episode_title: Defence Supply Chain: Rheinmetall Breaks Ground in Kassel

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Rheinmetall has broken ground on a thirty-eight thousand square metre logistics hub at Kassel Airport, before the big orders arrive.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Defence output is turning into network capacity in Germany. This is The Planning Desk.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Good morning, it's Friday the twenty-seventh of November, and I'm Anna.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: And I'm Erik.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Quick note, this show is made with A I. A I agents gather the news, and our voices are synthetic.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Today, Rheinmetall builds a hub in northern Hesse, two American drinks companies hedge fuel to steady freight costs, and Nvidia reportedly stops server shipments to four Southeast Asian markets.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: German defence group Rheinmetall and developer Panattoni have broken ground on the Defence Hub Kassel-Calden, produktion dot de reports. It's a logistics and training centre of thirty-eight thousand square metres, on a former airfield plot of about nine hectares at Kassel Airport.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: That's three months from site decision to spade in the ground. Up to two hundred new jobs are planned, and the first areas are due by the end of June twenty twenty-seven.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: When it picked the site in August, Rheinmetall said the hub would prepare the group for large military-vehicle orders from Germany and abroad.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: So the company is building its central node before the volumes arrive, and that's a network-design bet on the order book.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: It also moves the work for everyone around it. Suppliers in northern Hesse should expect call-offs, delivery points and lead-time agreements to be redrawn around Kassel from the middle of twenty twenty-seven.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: If you supply Rheinmetall, ask now where your parts will be delivered from next summer, and what that does to your transport plan and your safety stock.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Over in the U S, brewer Molson Coors and bottled-water maker Primo Brands are using fuel hedging to manage their logistics costs, Supply Chain Dive reports.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Experts quoted in the piece say hedging buys predictability, but it can be costly and hard to execute. The report gives no hedge volumes or savings.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: The catch sits in the plan. A hedge fixes the freight line in the budget, but it only pays if the volumes in your sales and operations plan, your S and OP, actually hold.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: So finance and planning have to agree the volume before treasury locks the price, or you end up paying for fuel on trucks you never send.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: Erik, the tech desk is yours.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: SAP has announced a collaboration with planqc, a quantum computing company based in Munich, according to SAP. It lets SAP develop directly on planqc's quantum hardware, with the aim of a shorter path to real business applications.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: The announcement names no use cases, no timelines and no performance figures.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Scheduling and network design are the usual first candidates for quantum. Until there's a use case on the table, treat this as a research signal from your E R P supplier, not a twenty twenty-seven planning tool.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: The biggest trade story of the day comes from chips. Following new U S export controls, Nvidia has reportedly told its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers with its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, The Loadstar reports, citing the Financial Times.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Dell and Supermicro have told buyers in the four countries about the halt. The U S rules aim to stop advanced chips reaching China through Southeast Asia.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: If your planning, analytics or A I workloads run in data centres there, ask your cloud and hosting providers which capacity is affected, and plan for it to sit in another region.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: On the freight desk, the Rhine at Kaub dropped to two hundred and seven centimetres, still far above what full barges need. And DHL says ocean rates are up a hundred and thirty-eight percent on last year, and expects shippers to put resilience ahead of price in the coming tender season.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Germany's procurement association B M E surveyed one thousand one hundred and forty-five buyers, and those who know databases and procurement software report notably higher median pay, so budget for that premium or train for it in-house.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: And on Tuesday, Swedbank and Silf publish the Swedish purchasing managers' index for November, a first read on factory inventories and delivery times going into December.

lines.speaker: F
lines.text: That's the desk for Friday.

lines.speaker: M
lines.text: Tomorrow it's the book of the week, and the full week in review is out on Sunday.

Rheinmetall is building its logistics hub before the big orders arrive, and suppliers will plan around it.

Rheinmetall and developer Panattoni have broken ground on the Defence Hub Kassel-Calden, a 38,000 m² logistics and training centre at Kassel Airport, produktion.de reports. The first areas are due by the end of June 2027, with up to 200 new jobs.

For suppliers in northern Hesse, expect call-offs, delivery points and lead-time agreements to be redrawn around Kassel from mid-2027.

Also on today's desk:
Molson Coors and Primo Brands hedge fuel to steady logistics costs, which only pays if S&OP volumes hold.
A BME survey of 1,145 procurement staff in Germany finds database and procurement-software skills come with higher median pay.

When a key customer opens a new hub, how early do you rework your delivery and stock plan?
